summary: When a thrown pyrolisk egg hits the stairs, C's breakobj() marks it for explosion, deletes the egg, then calls explode() with d(3,6) and EXPL_FIERY. JavaScript reaches an injected callback fallback and records explode.c explode instead of calling the existing explode implementation. The first divergence is segment 0 step 72: C logs d(3,6)=6 and draws the fiery explosion, while JavaScript continues without it.

source.branch: breakobj() handles EGG and sets explosion when corpsenm is PM_PYROLISK; after shop accounting and delobj(), it calls explode(x, y, -11, d(3,6), 0, EXPL_FIERY).
callers: dothrow.c:throwit() calls breakobj() after breaktest() and breakmsg() when a thrown object lands on a hard square; js/dothrow.js:throwit() already calls breakobj().
dothrow.c:hero_breaks() and breaks() call breakobj() after their break-test/message stages; js/dothrow.js exposes corresponding helpers.
do.c:lava_effects() and zap.c:fracture_rock() also call breakobj(); their existing JavaScript callers remain outside this selected egg branch.

evidence: nethack-c/upstream/src/dothrow.c:2525-2531 sets explosion only for an EGG whose corpsenm is PM_PYROLISK.
nethack-c/upstream/src/dothrow.c:2569-2573 first deletes the object when it is not a fracture, then calls explode(x,y,-11,d(3,6),0,EXPL_FIERY) before returning 1.

js/dothrow.js:1803-1810 substitutes rawEnv.explode and records note_unported('explode.c explode') when no callback is injected; the normal throwit caller passes only state and therefore skips C's explosion.
The existing js/explode.js exports explode(); dothrow.js already imports explode_oil from that module, so the C callee is available without a new source dependency.

The admitted v55 baseline reports 72/114 screens, 2583/2596 RNG calls, 112/114 cursors and error null. A bounded replay at the clean accepted baseline confirms the first difference at segment 0 step 72, key >, with C d(3,6)=6 @ breakobj and JavaScript rn2(12)=8.
